nodes.name: ZIF-67 disassembly in water bath
nodes.procedure: First, the synthesized ZIF-67 nanoparticles were partially disassembled in the 30°C water bath to open the small-sized windows (≈0.34 nm) of ZIF-67 by extracting partial Co²⁺ and 2-MIM components from the ZIF-67.
nodes.source_text: First, the synthesized ZIF-67 nanoparticles were partially disassembled in the 30°C water bath to open the small-sized windows (≈0.34 nm) of ZIF-67 by extracting partial Co²⁺ and 2-MIM components from the ZIF-67

nodes.name: POM-W encapsulation assembly
nodes.procedure: so that the POM-W (≈1 nm) molecules can easily access the cavities of ZIF-67 through the windows, resulting in the re-assembly into a POM-W/ZIF-67 composite.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal stabilization
nodes.procedure: Then the composite was further hydrothermally treated to stabilize the distribution of POM-W in ZIF-67 and strengthen the bonding between Co and W atoms.
nodes.source_text: Then the composite was further hydrothermally treated to stabilize the distribution of POM-W in ZIF-67...

nodes.name: Co-carbidization calcination
nodes.procedure: During calcination under N₂ atmosphere at 600°C, benefiting from the nanocage confinement of ZIF-67 and the chemical bonding between W and Co sources, a nanoparticulate Co₆W₆C compound (<20 nm) featuring a carbon polyhedron skeleton has been successfully synthesized. The 2-MIM component plays a role of a carbon source that bonds to both W and Co species, leading to the co-carbidization of the metal species into bimetallic carbide with deformed morphology.

unit_operations.name: Carbonization

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH (three-electrode setup)

C_dl.value: higher than Co-NC (0.48 mF/cm²) and W-NC (0.42 mF/cm²)

nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic performance... was studied comprehensively in 1M KOH electrolyte at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹... after 100% iR-correction... overpotentials of 50 and 187 mV to reach... 10 and 100 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope (40.99 mV dec⁻¹)... C_dl values... nearly 100% HER faradic efficiency... negligible degradation... during 10000 HER cycles, and almost no obvious decay... for up to 50 h

nodes.description: HER performance in simulated alkaline seawater (3M NaCl + 3M KOH) at 30°C
nodes.source_text: Co₆W₆C-2-600 achieves considerably low overpotentials for HER, featuring η₁₀ and η₁₀₀ values of 46 and 260 mV, respectively, at 30°C

nodes.description: HER performance in simulated alkaline seawater at 70°C
nodes.source_text: sample Co₆W₆C-2-600 possesses attractively low overpotentials at amplified current densities and elevated temperatures of 70°C, which is as low as 147 and 191 mV to reach 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻², respectively
sample Co₆W₆C-2-600 only requires an overpotential (η₁₀) of 290 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²... relatively smaller Tafel slope of 44.1 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: Overall water splitting electrolyzer in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: overall water splitting electrolyzer equipped with Co₆W₆C-2-600 as both anode and cathode catalysts could be operated at 1.56 V to reach a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²

nodes.description: Overall seawater electrolysis in simulated alkaline seawater at 30°C
nodes.source_text: the Co₆W₆C-2-600 catalyzed electrolyzer only requires 1.51 V to attain the current density of 10 mA cm⁻² at 30°C... excellent durability with the current retention rates of 104.7%... under 30°C
Mg/seawater battery... outputs a rather high open-circuit potential (OCV) of 1.71 V and a peak power density of up to 9.1 mW cm⁻²

nodes.description: Overall seawater electrolysis in simulated alkaline seawater at 70°C
nodes.source_text: the current density of the electrolyzer increases sharply with the increasing temperature, which needs 1.50 and 1.59 V to achieve 10 and 100 mA cm⁻² under 70°C, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₆W₆C-2-600 exhibits regular polyhedral morphology with crumpled surface anchored with uniform ultrasmall particles (<20 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co₆W₆C - 2 - 600 exhibits a regular polyhedral morphology and crumpled surface anchored with uniform ultrasmall particles (< 20 nm) (Figure 2e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₆W₆C-2-600 shows uniform ultrasmall particles (<20 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co₆W₆C - 2 - 600 exhibits a regular polyhedral morphology and crumpled surface anchored with uniform ultrasmall particles (< 20 nm) (Figure 2e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM demonstrates interplanar distances of 0.21 and 0.19 nm corresponding to the (511) and (440) planes of Co₆W₆C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) demonstrates interplanar distances of 0.21 and 0.19 nm corresponding to the (511) and (440) planes of Co₆W₆C (Figure 2g, A and B areas), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mappings show Co, W, C, N, and O are homogeneously dispersed in polyhedral Co₆W₆C-2-600.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the EDS elemental mappings in Figure 2h, the Co, W, C, N, and O are homogeneously dispersed in polyhedral Co₆W₆C - 2 - 600.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₆W₆C-2-600 demonstrates weak diffraction peaks at 43.08°, 47.12°, and 73.59° corresponding to the (511), (440) and (822) planes of Co₆W₆C (JCPDS No. 22-0597).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co₆W₆C - 2 -600 demonstrates weak diffraction peaks at 43.08°, 47.12°,and 73.59°, respectively corresponding to the (511), (440) and (822) planes of standard Co₆W₆C JCPDS No. 22-0597.

nodes.characterization_summary: Peak at 810 cm⁻¹ ascribed to W-C stretching mode in Co₆W₆C-600 based catalysts; peak at around 880 cm⁻¹ attributed to C-C stretching vibration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak position at 810 cm⁻¹ is ascribed to W-C stretching mode in Co₆W₆C - 600 based catalysts... the specific peak at around 880 cm⁻¹ is attributed to the C-C sketching vibration.

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ sorption isotherms show Co₆W₆C-600-based catalysts possess relatively large surface areas.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N₂ sorption isotherms of Co₆W₆C - 600 -based catalysts show that the obtained Co₆W₆C possesses relatively large surface areas (Figure 3c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₆W₆C-2-600 possesses the most negative charging of W atom (negative shift ≈0.25 eV) and highest Co²⁺ concentration (81.04%) among Co₆W₆C-600 catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co₆W₆C - 2 - 600 possesses the most negative charging of W atom among all Co₆W₆C - 600 catalysts, which show a negative shift up to ≈0.25 eV. Meanwhile... the Co₆W₆C - 2-600 has the highest Co²⁺ concentration (81.04%)

nodes.characterization_summary: W L₃ edge XANES shows white-line peak of Co₆W₆C-2-600 located between W foil and WO₃, indicating intermediate oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The white-line peak of (squared area) Co₆W₆C - 2 - 600 is located in between those of W foil and commercial WO₃ powder.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows peaks at ≈1.3 Å (W-O/C/N bonding) and ≈2.97 Å (W-Co/W bonding), confirming Co/W bimetallic carbide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks located at ≈1.3 Å originated from the W - O / C / N bonding, and the predominated peak at ≈2.97 Å could be assigned to W - Co / W bonding.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values of Co₆W₆C-600-based catalysts are much higher than Co-NC (0.48 mF cm⁻²) and W-NC (0.42 mF cm⁻²); Co₆W₆C-2-600 shows highest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl values of Co₆W₆C - 600 -based catalysts are much higher than those of Co-NC (0.48 mF cm⁻²) and W-NC (0.42 mF cm⁻²)

nodes.characterization_summary: Co₆W₆C-2-600 shows lowest charge-transfer resistance Rct = 4.08 Ω among Co₆W₆C-600 catalysts.
